newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Union, management meet at Neves Corvo copper mine.
newsitem.headline: Union, management meet at Neves Corvo copper mine.

text.p: Union leaders and management were meeting on Monday at Portugal's Neves Corvo copper mine where workers last week rejected the company's latest offer on working hours.
Company and union officials said the meeting began at 0900 GMT. They could not say how long it was due to last.

A meeting had initially been set for July 23 but the talks were brought forward after miners voted on Thursday against an improved company offer on the number of free days to be given in return for the introduction of Sunday shifts.
Miners at the 107,000 tonnes per year site stopped work for five days earlier this month after Somincor, the state-owned company that runs the mine, had sought to impose Sunday shifts.
Unions have accepted the principle of continuous working at the mine, some 250 km south of Lisbon, but want management to increase the additional benefits on offer.
Miners' leaders told Reuters last week there were no plans for a new strike providing the company kept talking to unions on the workers' demands.
